patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Tiendanube and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Tiendanube and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Tiendanube only if your buying job matches “LATAM hosted commerce (Tiendanube / Nuvemshop brand) — Argentina ARS tiles: Inicial $0, Es” rather than WooCommerce's shape. Choose WooCommerce only if your buying job matches “Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPaymen” rather than Tiendanube's shape. Workflow advantage: Tiendanube leans shared coverage; WooCommerce leans catalog-management. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Tiendanube and WooCommerce share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Tiendanube is LATAM hosted commerce (Tiendanube / Nuvemshop brand) — Argentina ARS tiles: Inicial $0, Esencial ~$20 USD, Impulso ~$59 highlighted, Escala ; WooCommerce is Open-source WordPress commerce plugin — free core; paid extensions, hosting, and WooPayments processing are separate TCO lines..
- Company-size focus: Tiendanube (small-business, mid-market) vs WooCommerce (solo, micro, small-business).
- Workflow coverage skew: Tiendanube-leaning — vs WooCommerce-leaning catalog-management.
- Researched limits: Tiendanube — Regional LATAM focus — not a global Shopify peer for every market; WooCommerce — You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS.

Limitations — Tiendanube: Regional LATAM focus — not a global Shopify peer for every market; USD amounts are FX approximates; ARS tiles are the source of truth; WooCommerce: You own hosting, security, updates, and plugin compatibility — operational burden vs SaaS; Extension sprawl can inflate TCO and maintenance.
